critical_code_review_comments: ledger.py: is_manual_bill keys only on trigger_type=='MANUAL'. manual_demand sets this for kind manual, other_charge and bounce, so bounce and other-charge bills raised through /demands/manual also count in Outstanding. This matches decision A as written; confirm the owner intends bounce charges to count too.

ledger.py: cancelled bookings still close the ledger. In rows, c_ord/a_ord = cash_paid/account_paid when closed and manual amounts are added only when not closed. In the final summary, a Cancelled status overrides to the paid amounts after manual totals are added. OK.

ledger.py, minor: rows use acc.closed, set by the CANCELLATION event, while the summary uses b.status=='Cancelled'. These agree unless a booking somehow has status Cancelled without a cancellation event (pre-existing, unchanged).
ledger.py: the FIFO demand-status loop puts manual bills into the per-bucket cumulative order by posted_at, so allocation order is unchanged as stated.
manual_demand sets cumulative_percent = max of previous demands. _demand then sets self.pct to that value, which is harmless (no plan % move).
integrity.py: summary raised is now compared with Σ all non-voided demands, which is consistent with summary.total_order_raised including manual bills.
read_models.recompute_all now also calls trends.on_dirty(project ids, set(), company ids), so monthly buckets are refreshed. OK.

portal.py portal_bulk_enable: hashing uses asyncio.to_thread under Semaphore(8). Duplicate phones in one batch and phones that already have accounts are skipped. The response shape {enabled, count} is unchanged. Remaining minor point: inserts are sequential and there is no catch for a DuplicateKey race with a concurrent enable (pre-existing).
